children: Remy Cointreau shares jumped after the French liquor group lifted its guidance for the fiscal year and set out a midterm plan, including job cuts, to shrug off the market weakness that has plagued the sector since the end of the pandemic.
In afternoon trading, shares were around 10% higher at 56.50 euros.

The company said Wednesday that it anticipates a return to sustainable organic sales growth over the fiscal year through March 2027, and now sees a solid organic improvement in its current operating margin compared with a slight improvement previously.

The maker of Remy Martin and Louis XIII cognac has struggled since a pandemic-led boom in alcohol consumption fizzled out, while economic headwinds in China have yet to pass. International trade disputes have added to costs and eaten into margins.

Under new medium-term targets, Remy Cointreau said it wants to grow organically by tapping demand in emerging markets and growing its presence in China. It is a growth strategy that relies on market-share gains rather than a recovery in the spirits market, Barclays analyst Laurence Whyatt wrote in a note.
The new targets are far below previously withdrawn expectations for fiscal 2030, which were issued during the heady days of the pandemic--when locked-down households splurged on expensive alcohol.

Remy Cointreau said it is now targeting average organic growth in the mid- to high-single digits into fiscal 2030 while achieving a current operating margin of over 22% in organic terms by fiscal 2032. The company is also targeting a reduction in its workforce by up to 15%, finance chief Luca Marotta told analysts in a call following the update.

In summer last year, the company withdrew its targets for fiscal 2030, citing a lack of macroeconomic visibility, a sluggish recovery in the U.S., and geopolitical uncertainties surrounding the U.S.'s and China's tariff policies.
Under the targets that were set out in June 2020, it had been aiming for a gross margin of 72% and a current operating margin of 33% in fiscal 2030.

The guidance uplift and targets came alongside sales for the first half of fiscal 2027 that grew 2.9% on an organic basis. Current operating profit rose nearly 8% on an organic basis to 126.7 million euros, equivalent to $138.9 million, giving it a margin of roughly 25%.
